translations.answer: The maintainer explicitly states that a single friction constraint is insufficient, a single CoP (center of pressure) constraint is also insufficient, and a contact wrench cone is required. The original author interpreted the wrench cone as encompassing friction, ZMP/CoP boundaries, and yaw torque boundaries, and the maintainer confirms this is correct. When using a wrench cone, the individual friction cone or CoP cost should be removed; the old example did not integrate it because it was written before the feature was available.
translations.applicability: Applicable to contact stability modeling in finite foot whole-body manipulation; current Crocoddyl API and constraint dimensions must be verified against the target version.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author reviewed the contact wrench cone paper and confirmed with the maintainer whether it covers friction, ZMP/CoP, and yaw torque boundaries.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author provided images of feet not aligned with the world coordinate system and asked for the rotation matrix.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Contact models require separate checks for tangential friction, CoP support domain, and yaw torque boundaries, rather than just seeing a friction cone and assuming full stability.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: The wrench cone constructor's first rotation parameter should be verified against the actual foot orientation.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use the contact wrench cone when the full finite foot constraint is required, and remove individual friction cones or CoP costs to avoid duplication.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: When feet are not aligned with the world frame, specify the rotation using the constructor of the wrench cone.
translations.details.environments.0: Crocoddyl whole_body_manipulation example, thread time from 2020-10 to 2021-02; no Crocoddyl version or robot model provided.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread does not provide specific API version, matrix direction convention, or code example for the contact wrench cone.
translations.details.limits.1: Cannot directly derive the rotation matrix from foot images; must return to the target version's constructor and reference system definition.
translations.details.limits.2: This discussion is from 2020/2021; the current Crocoddyl API name needs to be verified again.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author clarified the issue and stated they will update the example after the scheme is worked out; no subsequent implementation or numerical results are provided.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The rotation parameter issue is only mentioned by the maintainer in the interface, without author verification.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Is a friction cone or CoP/ZMP cost sufficient in whole-body manipulation? When should a contact wrench cone be used?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How should the wrench cone be oriented when the feet are not aligned with the world frame?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: In high dynamic real-world operations, monitor friction margin, CoP support domain, and yaw torque; an incorrect constraint reference system may result in seemingly feasible but non-executable contact forces.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The example was written before the contact wrench cone functionality was developed; the maintainer explains this is the reason for the example still using a friction cone, not indicating that it is sufficient.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Users cannot determine the relationship between friction cones, CoP/ZMP costs, and contact wrench cones in high dynamic whole-body operations.
translations.details.symptoms.1: When the foot has a yaw angle, users are unclear on how the wrench cone rotation matrix is defined.
translations.media_summaries.0: Comment 722446675's image has been verified: left is a photo of both feet, right is a diagram with Left foot, Right foot, support polygon, support polygon with margin, and Δx_zmp; the feet are not parallel; the image supports the question 'feet not aligned with the same world direction' but lacks coordinate axes or matrix definition, so it cannot be used to derive rotation parameters.
translations.source.locator: Crocoddyl #880: maintainer comment 718918420/718918724 gives the conclusion; comment 719454648 confirms the author's understanding and explains the cost combination; author 719600191 states the clarification.
translations.source.title: Configuration of contact wrench cone in Crocoddyl whole-body manipulation and foot rotation
